concerns.concern: The claim that Joule heating is excluded rests only on r0(P) being the same at 0.4 K and 5.6 K. A simple estimate gives a local temperature rise of order 1–3 K at 1 µm, so a quantitative thermal model (oxide on Si, temperature-dependent conductivity, boundary resistance) must be shown to fail before heating can be called excluded.
concerns.quote: The exclusion of Joule (thermal) heating rests on a single comparison of two temperatures, with no estimate of the expected temperature rise.

concerns.concern: The imaging works at µW powers and hundreds of nA of leakage, far above transport GCS experiments (pW to nW), possibly with oxide breakdown. Its link to transport GCS is assumed. Gate-dependent transport data (Ic(VG), Ic(P)) from device D1, ideally measured together with imaging, are needed.
concerns.quote: Device D1 was fabricated to mimic transport GCS devices, yet no gate-dependent transport data from D1 (or from the same film) appear in the main text.

concerns.concern: The authors' own hot-spot model should also give temperature-dependent Pd and rd, since the critical quasiparticle density and relaxation time vary strongly between 0.4 and 5.6 K. They need to explain the temperature independence and state the island Tc in the main text.
concerns.quote: the key observation used to exclude heating is not explained by the proposed alternative either.

concerns.concern: The quasiparticle lifetime of ~1e-9 s is stated in the abstract, yet the main text admits it cannot tell whether rd reflects quasiparticle diffusion in Nb or diffusion in the substrate. The lifetime should be removed from the abstract or stated as conditional on the quasiparticle channel.
concerns.quote: Please remove the lifetime from the abstract, or qualify it as conditional on the quasiparticle channel

concerns.concern: The fit uses a 3D isotropic diffusion equation. A 20 nm film is effectively 2D (K0 Green's function), and heat or phonons in an oxide on Si need a layered model. Fits with these alternative forms, with uncertainties and residuals, are requested.
concerns.quote: The functional form used therefore presupposes a channel the authors say they cannot identify.

concerns.concern: A good Lambert-W fit is weak evidence, because any monotonic sublinear two-parameter form would fit. A parameter-free prediction, e.g. for the corner, floating or extended-gate geometries, should be given in the main text with a number.
concerns.quote: Any monotonic, sublinear two-parameter form will fit Fig. 3a well. "Excellent agreement" is therefore weak support for the hot-spot picture specifically.

concerns.concern: The substrate diffusion channel is dismissed using the room-temperature thermal diffusivity of glass. That value is irrelevant at sub-K temperatures and for quasi-ballistic athermal phonons, so the estimate should be redone with appropriate parameters.
concerns.quote: That estimate uses the room-temperature thermal diffusivity of glass (1e-6 m^2/s, Ref. [29]). This is not the relevant quantity at sub-K temperatures

concerns.concern: In the floating-island geometry, suppression occurs with no current through the island, so energy must arrive via the substrate (or vacuum). This conflicts with dismissing the substrate channel.
concerns.quote: This argues for a substrate contribution and is in tension with dismissing that channel.

concerns.concern: The distinction between 'Joule heating' and 'non-equilibrium particles' is ill-defined, since leakage power is Joule dissipation either way. The real question is thermalized versus athermal energy delivery. The authors should say what observable separates the two, or admit that none currently does.
concerns.quote: The distinction between "Joule heating" and "non-equilibrium particles generated by the leakage current" needs a sharper definition.

concerns.concern: The conclusion that GCS is 'a genuine feature of superconductivity not restricted to transport' is too strong. What is shown is local suppression by leakage dissipation, which existing mechanistic work would predict. Greater energy needed to suppress screening over ~1 µm² could also explain the difference from transport.
concerns.quote: the claim that the GCS is "established as a genuine feature of superconductivity not restricted to transport" is too strong.

concerns.concern: The cooling protocol for each dataset is not stated. Under field cooling, changes in screening between panels may be due to vortex expulsion rather than GCS. This affects the comparison with vortex-free simulations and the Bx-step method, whose zero-gate reference map may contain vortices.
concerns.quote: Please state the cooling protocol (field-cooled or zero-field-cooled) for each dataset.

concerns.concern: All vortices are expelled at small gate power, when only a small fraction of the island is suppressed. This is consistent with global warming of the island reducing pinning. A control raising the bath temperature without gate power is requested.
concerns.quote: Please compare with a control in which the bath temperature is raised with no gate power, and check whether vortices leave at a comparable bath temperature.

concerns.concern: The claim that suppression is reproducible at the same power across all devices conflicts with fitted Pd differing by almost a factor of three between D3 and D2b. This needs reconciling and explaining, and uncertainties for rd and Pd should be given.
concerns.quote: the fitted Pd differs by almost a factor of three between D3 (0.95 uW) and D2b (0.36 uW), while rd is similar.

concerns.concern: The effective penetration depth (~2.9 µm) is comparable to the island size, so screening is nonlocal. A region of strongly reduced but nonzero superfluid density would look unscreened. 'Complete' suppression should only be claimed if a smooth suppression profile is excluded, and the sensitivity of r0 to the assumed profile should be shown.
concerns.quote: A region of strongly reduced, but nonzero, superfluid density would look nearly unscreened.

concerns.concern: The point-source-at-apex model ignores where the leakage power is actually dissipated. The leakage path (surface, through the oxide into Si, filament) could lie partly under the island, so the path and the fraction of power released near the apex should be discussed.
concerns.quote: Please discuss the leakage path explicitly ... and what fraction of P is dissipated near the apex.

concerns.concern: It is unclear whether r0 is measured from the gate apex or from the island edge. Since the apex is ~80 nm from the edge, the model implies a finite threshold power. Whether the zero-power point is included in the fit should be stated.
concerns.quote: How is r0 defined (from the apex or from the island edge)? Is the zero-power point included in the fit?

concerns.concern: Line cuts of measured Bz with model overlays are requested. Fig. 2b suggests screening of several hundred µT while the Fig. 2c color scale spans ±50 µT, raising the question of saturation and of the measured screening amplitude versus the model.
concerns.quote: Is the scale saturated, and what is the measured screening amplitude compared with the model?

concerns.concern: For D2a/D2b, scans used constant-current mode while VG drifted over hours. Scan duration, the variation of P during each image, and whether the quoted power uncertainties are the spread over the scan should be stated.
concerns.quote: Please state the duration of a scan and how much P varied during each image.

concerns.concern: Comparing the 0.7 ns lifetime with a hot-spot formation time from Ref. [13] is not a like-for-like comparison.
concerns.quote: The comparison of the 0.7 ns lifetime with a hot-spot formation time from Ref. [13] is also not like-for-like.

concerns.concern: Because P includes the 60 GΩ parasitic path, the authors should confirm that its contribution is negligible at the relevant gate voltages.
concerns.quote: Because P includes the 60 GOhm parasitic path, please also confirm that its contribution is negligible at the relevant VG

concerns.concern: The non-monotonic temperature dependence of the vortex escape power should be given with device and cool-down for each point, since field history can dominate.
concerns.quote: The non-monotonic temperature dependence of the escape power (0.45 K, 3.5 K, 5.8 K) should be stated with the device and cool-down for each

concerns.concern: Calling the suppressed region 'nanoscale' is misleading, since it exceeds 1 µm.
concerns.quote: Consider "micron-scale region imaged with nanoscale resolution".

concerns.concern: The outlook mixes temperature with gap energy and claims operation above Tc without showing above-Tc data. It should be rephrased, and the films' actual Tc given.
concerns.quote: Temperature and gap energy are mixed here, and no above-Tc data appear in the main text.

concerns.concern: Fig. 3b does not identify the temperature of each color or whether the two branches are different sweeps. A plot of point pairs at equal VG and different P would make the P-versus-VG point clearer.
concerns.quote: Fig. 3b: please state which temperature each color is, and whether the two branches correspond to different sweeps with different V_G^ON.

concerns.concern: The extended-gate argument about lower current density is qualitative, and the FEM maps show electric field, not current density. The authors should state what determines the current distribution in their leakage model.
concerns.quote: The E-field FEM maps in the top row show field, not current density.

concerns.concern: The explanation of the corner effect via the long penetration depth is underdeveloped. In a thin film the Pearl length is relevant, and the island edge also changes the diffusion boundary condition.
concerns.quote: Please expand. In a thin film the relevant length is the Pearl length

concerns.concern: Ref. [11] (spinons and spin-charge decoupling) is an inappropriate citation for quasiparticles from broken Cooper pairs; a textbook reference would be better.
concerns.quote: Ref. [11] (Kivelson and Rokhsar, spinons and spin-charge decoupling) is an unusual citation

concerns.concern: There are reference errors: Ref. [13] has an inconsistent DOI and year, Ref. [18] lacks a year, and Ref. [21] may need updating.
concerns.quote: Ref. [13]: the DOI (s41567-023-...) and the year (2021) are inconsistent. Ref. [18] lacks a year.

concerns.concern: There are typos, and the naming of thanked colleagues in the acknowledgments is inconsistent.
concerns.quote: Typos: "microcopy" (scanning tunneling microscopy), "enviroment", "the measured current include".

concerns.concern: The uncertainty notation '0.08(0) µW' in the Fig. 2c labels is odd.
concerns.quote: "0.08(0) uW" is odd notation for an uncertainty below the last digit.

concerns.concern: Since the measured SMU current includes wiring leakage, the authors should state for each device at which gate voltage device leakage dominates.
concerns.quote: Please state at which VG the device leakage dominates for each device.

concerns.concern: Data are available only on request. Raw scans and fit scripts should be deposited publicly, since the conclusions rest on model fits.
concerns.quote: deposition of the raw scans and fit scripts in a public repository would help
